_comment: Hand-written probability vectors. No audio, no model, no GPU, no library.
Each case is a set of per-window language probabilities and the verdict the
settle rules must reach from them. The whole ladder is decidable from this
file, which is the point: the part most likely to be subtly wrong is the
part that needs no media to test, and a threshold that can only be checked
by another pass over terabytes never gets checked.
'tag' is what the file already claims. 'speech_total_s' is present only
where the no-speech rule is under test. 'prior' and 'support' describe the
context and the corroboration the later stages would have produced.

cases.name: a unanimous run confirms the tag that is already there
cases.why: Rule A: confirming is cheap and writes nothing, so one agreeing window is enough.

cases.name: a weak run still confirms an existing tag it agrees with
cases.why: The evidence is thin, but it points the same way as the tag and nothing is written.

cases.name: an untagged track settles on strong agreement
cases.why: The standard bar: enough counted windows, confident, clear of the runner-up, agreed.

cases.name: three confident windows are not enough on a long item
cases.why: A feature-length item can supply five; accepting three would be accepting less evidence than was available.

cases.name: an item too short for five windows settles on three unanimous ones
cases.why: Demanding five windows from a sixty-second clip is demanding the impossible; the bar rises instead.

cases.name: contradicting a tag at the standard bar is refused
cases.why: The asymmetry, stated: this evidence would settle an untagged track and is not enough to overturn one.

cases.name: contradicting a tag is accepted once the higher bar is cleared
cases.why: Eight counted windows, near-certainty and unanimity. An overturn rewrites what somebody chose.

cases.name: one strongly disagreeing window collapses the score
cases.why: The geometric mean, and the reason for it: five complacent windows do not outvote one that is certain.

cases.name: two languages splitting the windows is a conclusion, not a failure
cases.why: A track that is genuinely two languages cannot be described by one tag, so it never becomes a write.

cases.name: a track with almost no speech in it is not a language question
cases.why: Under a minute of speech in a whole track: the answer is that there is no linguistic content, and that is writable.

cases.name: a strong prior that agrees lowers the audio bar
cases.why: Rule B. The prior never speaks for the audio; it lets slightly weaker audio be enough.

cases.name: a prior that points the other way changes nothing
cases.why: A prior can only ever agree with the audio. Against it, it is not evidence, it is a guess.

cases.name: a prior blocked by the material is not used at all
cases.why: Commentary, extras, specials and clips are where context is systematically misleading.

cases.name: one foreign-language scene is trimmed, with corroboration
cases.why: Rule C. Two windows legitimately disagree; the rest are unanimous, and two independent stages agree.

cases.name: the same evidence without corroboration does not settle
cases.why: Without the two stages, trimming is a licence to discard the inconvenient windows.

cases.name: a window with no speech in it does not get a vote
cases.why: A music-only window still produces a language vector, and averaging it in is how silence acquires an opinion.

cases.name: codes that mean nothing are not tags
cases.why: An undetermined tag is the absence of a claim, so settling one is a settle and not an overturn.

cases.name: a tag spelled the other way is the same tag
cases.why: Two spellings of one language are not a disagreement, and treating them as one proposes a pointless write.
